qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what sequence of evidence established that the groin catheter was the source of a bloodstream infection rather than only a local site infection?
qas.answer: Staph in blood plus matching catheter tip/wound cultures.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, why did the team remove the left groin tunneled dialysis catheter early rather than trying to treat through it?
qas.answer: Suspected infected dialysis catheter; removal is safest source control.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, how did the initial gram stain result justify continuing vancomycin before final speciation and sensitivities returned?
qas.answer: Gram-positive cocci suggested staph; vancomycin covers MRSA.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what timing relationship between catheter removal and follow-up blood cultures supported that the infection was being controlled?
qas.answer: Post-removal repeat blood cultures stayed negative.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what was the clinical rationale for a short “line holiday” before placing a new tunneled dialysis catheter?
qas.answer: Allow treatment and confirm blood cultures clear before new line.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what combination of findings prompted evaluation for endocarditis despite clinical improvement?
qas.answer: MRSA bacteremia prompted TEE to rule out valve seeding.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what two unexpected TEE findings changed management of the newly placed right groin dialysis catheter?
qas.answer: Catheter tip crossed ASD into left atrium; mobile tip clot.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, why was a heparin drip started and then a repeat TEE performed shortly afterward?
qas.answer: To treat suspected catheter-tip clot and confirm it resolved.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, how did the doctor address the patient’s fear that HIV would worsen outcomes from the catheter infection?
qas.answer: Acknowledged immunosuppression; emphasized stable vitals and early treatment.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what is the most likely reason emtricitabine was scheduled only after dialysis on Monday and Friday while other antiretrovirals were daily?
qas.answer: Renal failure/hemodialysis requires reduced, post-dialysis dosing.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, what clinical reasoning linked the onset of watery diarrhea to a specific hospital-acquired infection and led to immediate precautions?
qas.answer: Recent antibiotics raised C. diff concern; contact precautions started.

qas.question: During the hospitalization from 2131-12-17 to 2131-12-24, why was long-term warfarin not started despite cardiology recommending anticoagulation?
qas.answer: Patient declined due to monitoring burden; team deferred to outpatient follow-up.
